title: Liv Morgan Discusses Real-Life Heat Between Wrestlers - NewsBreak
text:
By Ryan Clark ,
44 minutes ago Liv Morgan has become one of WWE’s biggest stars, but the former Women’s World Champion admits she wasn’t a natural in the ring when she first entered the company. In fact, Morgan believes she might not have survived WWE’s current developmental system if she had received her opportunity today rather than in 2014.
During a recent appearance on “Hot Ones with Sean Evans,” Morgan discussed whether growing up as a passionate WWE fan gave her an advantage when she began training. While she initially believed her lifelong love of wrestling would translate into immediate success, she quickly discovered that watching wrestling and performing it were two very different things.
Morgan said she had been obsessed with WWE since she was five years old and expected to thrive as soon as she stepped into the wrestling business. She said,
“For me, like, no advantage. Such the illusion of an advantage. I thought I was gonna walk in there and be a natural. I thought I was gonna absolutely kill it. I’ve been a fan since I was five years old, like, eat, sleep, breathe, loved WWE. Would come home from school, take a nap, and if I missed five minutes it, I’m waking up crying and screaming. Like, I was obsessed with WWE. I thought when I started, I was gonna be champion in, like, a year.”
“I was like, ‘This is gonna be,’ not a piece of cake but I was like, ‘This is my life.’ So hard. And I feel like back then, you were given a lot of grace. Like, they would give you awhile to try to get good so I’m so grateful that I started when I did ’cause I think if I started now, I don’t think I would’ve made the cut ’cause they gave me a lot of time to develop and train and learn.”

Asked by Evans whether real-life disagreements between wrestlers make their matches better or worse, Morgan explained that a genuine lack of respect can become obvious when the performers are working together. She said,
“I’ve seen scenarios where there is a lack of respect and it translates in the ring in weird ways where you can tell that they do not like each other, they are not working together, or their promo segments where they are saying things that are not on script, that are not in, like, kayfabe, you know? And it doesn’t end well, you know, ultimately, things get patched up.”
“But I like to think that if someone doesn’t like me, they know I’m gonna’ give them an amazing match regardless at the end of the day and so they’re not worried about whatever issues that we’re having.”
“Total pro. Total pro. Total pro. Total pro. I don’t think I could be more of a pro. I think I’m, like, the pro-est.”
Morgan also shared how her perspective on one of her favorite childhood television shows has changed as she has gotten older.
During the same “Hot Ones” appearance, the WWE star discussed Boy Meets World and explained why she no longer views Cory Matthews as the ideal boyfriend she once believed him to be. She said,
“It’s just, like, a show for the times, ‘Boy Meets World’, but you know I do watch it back and I have a complete different perspective of it than I did watching it. Like I remember I thought Cory was, like, so romantic, such a good guy, great guy for Topanga, like when she chose not to go to Yale and choose Cory, I was like, ‘Yeah, like, love.’”
“But now when I watch it back as a grown woman, I’m like, ‘This man is manipulative. He’s toxic. He’s gaslighting the sh** out of her.’ B**ch, you’re not gonna go to Yale for Cory?”
“And so I feel like my perspective of it has changed but I think it was just one of those shows. Like, ‘Saved by the Bell’, just like nostalgic, group of friends.”
“Coming-of-age. Like ‘The Wonder Years’. Do you watch ‘The Wonder Years’?”
